title: `rig proj sync` re-runs entirely under sudo when it installs R in admin mode, so the project library is owned by root
description:
In admin mode on Linux, when `rig proj sync` has to install the project's R version, the whole `rig proj sync` command is re-run under `sudo`, not only the R installation. The packages are then installed as root into the project's `.rvenv/lib`, using a package cache under `/root/.cache/rig`.

rig 0.11.1 (`rig-linux-x86_64-0.11.1.tar.gz`), Ubuntu 24.04, admin mode, no R installed.

To reproduce, as a normal user with passwordless sudo (I used a `ubuntu:24.04` container):

```sh
mkdir proj && cd proj
rig proj init -r 4.6
rig proj add --no-lock cli
rig proj lock
rig proj sync --locked
ls -ld .rvenv .rvenv/lib
ls -l .rvenv/lib
```

```
[INFO] RIG START [pid:2167] rig proj sync --locked
[INFO] /home/user/.cache/rig/p3m/p3m-status.json is up to date, skipping download
R 4.6.2 (x86_64) is not installed, installing it now
Running `sudo` for adding new R versions. This might need your password.
[INFO] RIG START [pid:2170] /opt/rig/bin/rig proj sync --locked
[INFO] Checking for updates for /root/.cache/rig/p3m/p3m-status.json
R 4.6.2 (x86_64) is not installed, installing it now
...
1 of 1 packages to install (/home/user/proj/.rvenv/lib)
[INFO] Installed built package cli 3.6.6 from /root/.cache/rig/packages/bin/linux/noble-x86_64/4.6/cli_3.6.6-20e4b277.tar.gz into /home/user/proj/.rvenv/lib
Deployment complete, installed 1 packages

drwxr-xr-x  5 root root 4096 Nov  5 16:47 .rvenv
drwxr-xr-x  3 root root 4096 Nov  5 16:47 .rvenv/lib
drwxr-xr-x 11 root root 4096 Nov  5 16:47 cli
```

We hit this on GitHub Actions (`ubuntu-24.04`), where passwordless sudo means nothing prompts and the problem only shows up when a later step tries to write to the library: `rig pkg install --library <project>/.rvenv/lib` run as the normal user fails, as the library belongs to root.

From what I can tell, `proj sync` installs R in-process through `sc_add()`, which calls `escalate("adding new R versions")`, and `sudo::with_env()` re-runs the current command line (`std::env::args()`) under `sudo` and then exits. So everything after the R installation also runs as root.

https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/c9df020f02a8b0ab43ccca1f5963700a46800868/src/proj.rs#L5054-L5070

https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/c9df020f02a8b0ab43ccca1f5963700a46800868/src/linux.rs#L288-L290

I expected only the R installation to be elevated, and the packages to be installed as the invoking user, like when R is already installed. Is this intended ? Please correct me if I'm reading it wrong. I only tried Linux; `src/macos.rs` escalates the same way for `rig add`, but I haven't checked macOS.

As a workaround we now run `rig add 4.6` as its own step, then `rig proj sync --locked --no-install-r`.

title: `rig pkg install` doesn't show why a package failed when the error happens before `R CMD INSTALL` (e.g. permission denied on the library)
description:
When a package fails to install because of an error before `R CMD INSTALL` runs, `rig pkg install` does not say why. The output only has the final count, and the underlying error (here `Permission denied`) is only visible with `-v`.

rig 0.11.1 (`rig-linux-x86_64-0.11.1.tar.gz`), Ubuntu 24.04.

To reproduce, with a library directory the current user cannot write to:

```sh
sudo mkdir lib
rig pkg install --library ./lib cli
```

```
Installing 1 packages.
[INFO] Installing 1 packages in dependency order with max_concurrent=8
[INFO] Installing package cli from /home/user/.cache/rig/packages/src/cli_3.6.6-f4a1deb1.tar.gz to ./lib
[ERROR] Installation completed: 0 succeeded, 1 failed
Error: Installation completed with 1 failures (0 succeeded)
```

With `rig -v`, there is one more line:

```
[2026-11-05T16:55:00Z DEBUG src/install.rs:838] Install task completed with error for cli: Permission denied (os error 13)
```

Even then, the path it could not write to is not shown.

With several packages it is harder to follow, as the dependents are reported but not the root failure. This is from our CI on GitHub Actions, where the library was most likely owned by root after a `rig proj sync` (#503):

```
[INFO] Installing package htmltools from /home/runner/.cache/rig/packages/src/htmltools_0.5.9.9000-90a5dee5.tar.gz to /home/runner/work/project/tests/.rvenv/lib
[ERROR] Skipping package rmarkdown because a dependency failed
[ERROR] Skipping package bslib because a dependency failed
[ERROR] Skipping package fontawesome because a dependency failed
[ERROR] Skipping package sass because a dependency failed
[INFO] Installing package xfun from /home/runner/.cache/rig/packages/bin/linux/noble-x86_64/4.6/xfun_0.62-4783e8b7.tar.gz to /home/runner/work/project/tests/.rvenv/lib
[ERROR] Skipping package tinytex because a dependency failed
[ERROR] Installation completed: 0 succeeded, 7 failed
Error: Installation completed with 7 failures (0 succeeded)
```

Nothing says that htmltools and xfun failed, nor why.

From what I can tell, an `R CMD INSTALL` failure is reported (`Failed to install <pkg>` with the log path), but any error returned earlier with `?` in `r_cmd_install()`, for example creating `<library>/_logs`, only reaches the `debug!()` in the install task, and the main loop drops it:

https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/c9df020f02a8b0ab43ccca1f5963700a46800868/src/install.rs#L569-L570

https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/c9df020f02a8b0ab43ccca1f5963700a46800868/src/install.rs#L934-L940

https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/c9df020f02a8b0ab43ccca1f5963700a46800868/src/install.rs#L983-L985

I tested 0.11.1 only. I see that dc3f23c improved the failure summary on `main`, but reading the code it looks like these errors are still only logged at debug level there. Please correct me if I'm reading it wrong.

I expected rig to print the error for the package that failed, e.g. `Failed to install cli: Permission denied (os error 13)` with the path, like it does for an `R CMD INSTALL` failure.

title: rvenv shim: "already activated" check is always FALSE on Windows, so child R processes re-read ~/.Renviron
description:
On Windows, the `rvenv` shim never recognises that a parent process already activated the project. A child R process started in the project root then re-reads `~/.Renviron`, and it overwrites any variable the parent changed that `~/.Renviron` also sets. In an unsynced project, the child also warns "Project is not synced" a second time.

From what I can tell, this comes from how `venv` is built in `.onLoad()`:

https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/2260eb7c8054eec84055d7295568636bd0bfa252/src/data/rvenv-pkg/R/rvenv.R#L38-L53

On Windows `normalizePath()` returns backslashes and `file.path()` then adds a forward slash, so `venv` is `C:\Users\user\my-project/.rvenv`. The other side of the comparison goes through `normalizePath()` and gives `C:\Users\user\my-project\.rvenv`, so `identical()` is `FALSE` even when `RVENV` points at this project. The same happens for `RVENV_UNSYNCED`:

https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/2260eb7c8054eec84055d7295568636bd0bfa252/src/data/rvenv-pkg/R/rvenv.R#L76-L81

https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/2260eb7c8054eec84055d7295568636bd0bfa252/src/data/rvenv/onload.R#L55-L62

So `activated` is always `FALSE` and `readRenviron(home_renv)` runs in every child:

https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/2260eb7c8054eec84055d7295568636bd0bfa252/src/data/rvenv-pkg/R/rvenv.R#L60-L61

Please correct me if I'm reading it wrong.

## Reproduction

rig 0.11.1, R 4.5.2, Windows 11. With this line in `~/.Renviron`:

```
RIG_PROBE=from_home_renviron
```

In a new directory:

```
rig proj init
rig proj sync
```

and a `parent.R` in the project root:

```r
venv <- file.path(normalizePath(getwd()), ".rvenv")
print(venv)
print(normalizePath(Sys.getenv("RVENV"), mustWork = FALSE))
print(identical(normalizePath(Sys.getenv("RVENV"), mustWork = FALSE), venv))

Sys.setenv(RIG_PROBE = "set_by_parent")
system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript.exe"), c("-e", "cat(Sys.getenv('RIG_PROBE'))"))
```

```
> .\.rvenv\bin\Rscript.exe parent.R
[1] "C:\\Users\\user\\my-project/.rvenv"
[1] "C:\\Users\\user\\my-project\\.rvenv"
[1] FALSE
from_home_renviron
```

The child prints `from_home_renviron`, not `set_by_parent`. It is the same with plain `Rscript.exe parent.R` started in the project root, without the wrapper.

For the warning, in a project after `rig proj init` only (no sync):

```
> Rscript.exe -e "invisible(system2(file.path(R.home('bin'), 'Rscript.exe'), c('-e', '1')))"
! Project is not synced. Run: rig proj sync
! Project is not synced. Run: rig proj sync
[1] 1
```

## One question

While looking at this, I noticed the `.rvenv\bin` wrappers set `RVENV` before R starts. If I read `R.sh` correctly, on macOS and Linux its `RVENV` already equals `venv`, so a session started from the wrapper counts as `activated` there and does not re-read `~/.Renviron`. I have not tested that on macOS or Linux. On Windows, once the comparison matches, wrapper-started sessions would behave the same way. Is that intended for a top-level wrapper session, or should only child processes skip `~/.Renviron` ?

I'm happy to test anything on Windows.

title: User-mode R ignores the system CA store, so package installs fail behind a TLS-inspecting proxy
description:
### I Have checked the following

- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for similar issues

### Bug description

In user mode, `rig add` downloads the Mozilla bundle from curl.se.
It then writes `SSL_CERT_FILE` and `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` into the `Renviron.site` of each R version, pointing at that file.
R reads `Renviron.site` at startup, so these values override anything the user exports in the shell.

On a network that inspects TLS, the proxy certificate is in the system store but not in the rig bundle.
R's libcurl then rejects every HTTPS download, while the system `curl` works.
The `curl` R package and `httr2` also work, because they use the system store.
#227 and #295 are about rig's own HTTP client, not about R.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `rig system user-mode`, then `rig add release`.
2. Put the CA certificate of the proxy in `/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/` and run `update-ca-certificates`.
3. Check that `curl -I https://cloud.r-project.org` succeeds.
4. Run `Rscript -e 'options(internet.info = 0); download.file("https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES", tempfile())'`.

### Actual behaviour

```text
*  CAfile: /home/user/.local/share/rig/etc/cacert.pem
* SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
Error in download.file(...) :
  URL 'https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES': status was 'SSL peer certificate or SSH remote key was not OK'
```

`install.packages()` and `renv` fail the same way.
`SSL_CERT_FILE` in `~/.bashrc` has no effect.
A `~/.Renviron` works only outside a project, because R reads the project `.Renviron` instead of it.
`rig system update-certs` replaces the bundle, so manual additions are lost.

### Expected behaviour

R should trust the certificates that the user already trusts system-wide.
Alternatively, rig could offer a setting to append extra certificates to its bundle, and `rig system update-certs` would keep them.

### Your environment

- rig 0.11.0 in user mode, R 4.5.3
- Ubuntu 24.04 on WSL2
- Terminal and Rscript, no IDE involved

title: rig pkg install fails for git/GitHub and url:: sources on Windows: \\?\ verbatim path passed to R CMD INSTALL
description:
I've run into issues installing dev versions of packages or my personal non-CRAN packages off of GitHub using `rig pkg install {url}`. Full disclosure, the below issue was generated with Opus 5.5.

## Summary

On Windows, `rig pkg install` fails for any git/GitHub or `url::` package source. rig passes the fetched source directory to `R CMD INSTALL` as a verbatim (`\\?\`-prefixed) path, and R rejects it as an "invalid package". Binary dependencies install fine, and CRAN source packages (`--platform source`) also install fine.

This is a regression from 6a350b5 (first released in v0.10.0) and is still present on `main`.

## Reproduce

```
rig pkg install --library $env:TEMP\rig-reprex-lib tidyverse/dplyr
```

Output (trimmed):

```
Fetching dplyr from https://github.com/tidyverse/dplyr.git
Fetched dplyr
Downloading 14 packages
Installing 15 packages.
Error: Failed to install dplyr
  See log: C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp\rig-reprex-lib\_logs\dplyr-install.log
[ERROR] Installation failed for dplyr from C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\gaborcsardi\rig\cache\packages\git/github/tidyverse/dplyr/d5e94e7fa8fd4a5f79c1a707d1842216bb4c691f: exit code 1
Error: Installation completed with 1 failures (14 succeeded)
```

`dplyr-install.log`:

```
Warning: invalid package '\\?\C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\gaborcsardi\rig\cache\packages\git\github\tidyverse\dplyr\d5e94e7fa8fd4a5f79c1a707d1842216bb4c691f'
Error: ERROR: no packages specified
```

A `url::` source fails the same way:

```
rig pkg install --library $env:TEMP\rig-reprex-lib --no-cache url::https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/praise_1.0.0.tar.gz
```
```
Warning: invalid package '\\?\C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp\rig-nocache-18016\packages\url\5c035e74...\praise'
Error: ERROR: no packages specified
```

whereas `rig pkg install --platform source praise` (CRAN tarball) succeeds.

## Root cause

`r_cmd_install()` canonicalizes both paths before calling R ([src/install.rs#L541-L542](https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/v0.11.0/src/install.rs#L541-L542), added in 6a350b5 to run R from a temp dir):

```rust
let library_path_abs = library_path.canonicalize()?;
let package_path_abs = package_path.canonicalize()?;
```

On Windows, `std::fs::canonicalize()` always returns a verbatim `\\?\` path. `tools:::.install_packages()` accepts a directory argument only if `file.exists(file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION"))` is TRUE. `file.path()` joins with `/`, and Win32 does not normalize forward slashes in `\\?\` paths, so the check fails even though the directory exists:

```r
p <- "\\\\?\\C:\\Users\\<user>\\AppData\\Local\\gaborcsardi\\rig\\cache\\packages\\git\\github\\tidyverse\\dplyr\\d5e94e7fa8fd4a5f79c1a707d1842216bb4c691f"
dir.exists(p)                                  #> TRUE
file.exists(file.path(p, "DESCRIPTION"))       #> FALSE   <- what R CMD INSTALL checks
file.exists(paste0(p, "\\DESCRIPTION"))        #> TRUE
```

CRAN source packages are unaffected because their path is a `.tar.gz` file, which R untars without joining a path onto it. Git and `url::` sources are unpacked directories, so they hit the `file.path()` check.

The `-l` library path is canonicalized the same way, so it will likely cause a similar failure once the package path is fixed.

## Environment

- rig 0.11.0
- R 4.5.0 (2025-04-11 ucrt)
- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200

title: Override .gitignored *.rds files in .rvenvlib
description:
A rig project has to commit the rvenv shim in .rvenvlib/rvenv/, and that shim includes Meta/package.rds. I frequently have `*.rds` in my projects' `.gitignore` files because they keep cached data and model objects as rds files. So git silently leaves out Meta/package.rds, so the committed shim is incomplete.  In this case, a clone or worktree of the project fails to load the project library. I suspect there are a lot of such projects. 

Some possible fixes:
 - rig proj init adds a `.gitignore` to `.rvenvlib/` that overrides a project-level `.gitignore` of key files/types.
-  The startup warning names the likely cause, e.g. "rvenv shim in .rvenvlib is incomplete; is part of it gitignored?"
-  The project setup docs mention that .rvenvlib/ must be committed in full, and that this can clash with *.rds ignore rules

rig 0.11.0
R 4.6 (aarch64-apple-darwin)
macOS (Darwin 25.6)
Found through git worktree add; a fresh git clone should behave the same.

title: macOS user mode: Cairo SVG plots cannot locate bundled fontconfig configuration
description:
With rig's user-mode R installation on macOS, `svg()` reports a fontconfig error and renders plot text as boxes. The bundled `fonts.conf` exists, but R does not locate it automatically.

Environment:

- rig 0.10.0, configured with `mode=user`
- macOS 26.6.2, arm64
- R 4.6.0 (2026-04-24)
- R installed under `~/.local/share/rig/r/4.6.0`
- Neither `FONTCONFIG_FILE` nor `FONTCONFIG_PATH` is set

### Reproducible example

Run in a terminal:

```sh
Rscript --vanilla -e '
print(file.exists(file.path(R.home(), "fontconfig/fonts/fonts.conf")))
svg("font-test.svg")
plot(1:3, main = "Font rendering test", xlab = "x", ylab = "y")
dev.off()
'
```

Output:

```text
[1] TRUE
Fontconfig error: Cannot load default config file: No such file: (null)
null device
          1
```

The SVG is created, but its text appears as boxes.

### Expected behavior

The plot should render readable text using the configuration bundled with the user-mode R installation, without additional graphics-device settings.

### Diagnostic comparison

The same plot works when explicitly selecting the bundled configuration in a fresh R process:

```sh
Rscript --vanilla -e '
Sys.setenv(
  FONTCONFIG_FILE = file.path(R.home(), "fontconfig/fonts/fonts.conf")
)
svg("font-test-configured.svg")
plot(1:3, main = "Font rendering test", xlab = "x", ylab = "y")
dev.off()
'
```

This produces readable text without the fontconfig error.

### Possible cause

The installed `library/grDevices/libs/cairo.so` contains the path `/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/fontconfig/fonts`, which does not exist on my machine.

In [`src/macos.rs`](https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/main/src/macos.rs), `patch_user_scripts()` updates paths inside the relocated `fonts.conf`, and `replace_user_fontconfig()` sets `FONTCONFIG_FILE` for `fc-cache`. Could R startup need a corresponding setting so Cairo finds the relocated configuration?

title: rig fails with "No such file or directory" in user mode on macOS when ~/.local/bin does not exist
description:
On macOS in user mode, when `~/.local/bin` does not exist yet, most rig commands fail with a bare error:

```
$ rig list
✗ No such file or directory (os error 2)
$ rig add 4.6.1 --user
✗ No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

A fresh macOS user account has no `~/.local/bin`, so this is the state of anyone who has not installed R with rig before (and has not had some other tool create that directory). Reproduced with rig 0.11.0 and with `main` (d8054fc):

```sh
H=$(mktemp -d)
HOME=$H RIG_MODE=user rig list          # fails
mkdir -p $H/.local/bin
HOME=$H RIG_MODE=user rig list          # works
```

Cause: `find_aliases()` in `src/macos.rs` calls `std::fs::read_dir()` on the binary directory without checking that it exists. `sc_get_list_details()` calls it for `rig list`, and `rig add` calls it through `find_installed_version_arch()` for the already-installed check, before anything has had a chance to create the directory (`sc_set_default` and `sc_system_make_links` create it, but they run later). The Linux and Windows versions of `find_aliases()` already return an empty list when the directory is missing, so this is macOS only.

Impact: RStudio now bundles rig and runs `rig add <version> --user` when a project asks for an R version that is not installed (rstudio/rstudio#19229). On a Mac without `~/.local/bin` that install fails with the message above and nothing else to go on. Workaround until then: `mkdir -p ~/.local/bin`.

This is not #462, which is admin mode and `rig library list`, although the error text is the same.

title: apt repo signing key rotation broke install instructions; documented `rig.gpg` URL returns 404
description:
Potential dupe #296 seems different.
-----
# What happened

Following the canonical Ubuntu/Debian install at
[`website/_partials/install-methods.md` (lines 238-240)](https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/main/website/_partials/install-methods.md)
on Linux Mint 22.3 (Ubuntu 24.04 noble), the key fetch step fails:

    curl -L https://rig.r-pkg.org/deb/rig.gpg -o /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/rig.gpg
    # HTTP/2 404

Subsequent `apt update` reports:

    W: GPG error: http://rig.r-pkg.org/deb rig InRelease: The following
       signatures couldn't be verified because the public key is not available:
       NO_PUBKEY 6C439202CCDB438D

## Root cause

The previously documented signing key (Gabor Csardi, fingerprint
`58E396DE9104D88142576CE32D0A34BD1C5AF134`) **expired 2026-08-31**.

The current `InRelease` is signed with the new key fingerprint
`52F30566E548B8F23A93507F6C439202CCDB438D` (short ID `6C439202CCDB438D`),
but the new key has not been republished at the documented URL:

    $ curl -I https://rig.r-pkg.org/deb/rig.gpg
    HTTP/2 404

Verified:

- `gpg --verify InRelease` -> `using RSA key 52F30566E548B8F23A93507F6C439202CCDB438D`,
  issuer `csardi.gabor@gmail.com`
- the new key is **absent** from common public keyservers (keyserver.ubuntu.com,
  keys.openpgp.org, pgp.mit.edu)

## Existing-install impact

The rig binary does not embed a fallback public key
(`strings /usr/local/bin/rig | grep -E '52F30566|6C439202'` returns nothing),
so existing users have no automatic path to recovery. Every apt user who
installed rig via the documented flow has been broken since 2026-08-31
unless they manually fetched the new key.

## Workaround discovered

The new key is published in this very repo at
[`containers/ubuntu/rig.gpg`](https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/main/containers/ubuntu/rig.gpg)
(binary GPG keyblock, ~1160 bytes). It is used by the project's own Docker
setup:

    # containers/ubuntu/Dockerfile
    COPY rig.gpg /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/rig.gpg

Affected users can recover with:

    sudo curl -fsSL \
      "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/r-lib/rig/main/containers/ubuntu/rig.gpg" \
      -o /etc/apt/keyrings/rig.gpg
    sudo chmod 0644 /etc/apt/keyrings/rig.gpg

Fingerprint of that file matches the `InRelease` signer -- verified.

## Suggested fixes

Any one of these would close the loop:

1. **Republish the new key at the documented URL** --
   `https://rig.r-pkg.org/deb/rig.gpg` returns 404 right now; restoring
   the file there fixes new installs without docs changes.
2. **Update `install-methods.md`** to fetch from the GitHub source and
   prefer the modern `/etc/apt/keyrings/` + `[signed-by=...]` layout
   over `/etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/` (more security too).
3. **Embed the public key in the `rig` binary** so future rotations
   have an automatic recovery path. Today the binary has zero
   fingerprint-string match.

`NEWS.md` (top entry `rig 0.11.0-beta`) does not mention the rotation either.

## Environment

- `rig` 0.10.0 (apt-installed `r-rig`)
- Linux Mint 22.3 Zena / Ubuntu 24.04 noble
- apt 2.7.x
- Detected today (2026-10-05)

title: Repository types
description:
We'll need to introduce explicit repository types in rig, to optimize how we handle them. There are at least three types:

1. Repos with extended metadata, i.e. tidyup 12, like the ones I created for P3M at [ppm.r-pkg.org](http://ppm.r-pkg.org/).
2. (Typical) R-universe, where package files are replaced without even changing the version numbers, but there is some extra metadata with a custom API.
3. Plain CRAN-like repos, with older packages still available in Archive/ (with some metadata about them), like CRAN proper. Metadata might have SHA256 or MD5 hashes.
4. Bioconductor. Essentially like 3. but it is a family of repos and we need to choose between then based on R version. Maybe not a separate type.
5. Plain CRAN-like repos without Archive/. Metadata might still have SHA256 or MD5 hashes. Maybe not a separate type.

title: Proposal: add rig proj renv migrate and improve renv import
description:
## Motivation

Writing the renv-to-rig tutorial in [#470](https://github.com/r-lib/rig/pull/470) exposed how much of the migration users currently have to coordinate themselves. Would a `rig proj renv migrate` command be useful? This issue proposes follow-up CLI work; the linked PR adds documentation only.

The existing import converts exact versions to compatible-version requirements, does not retain package-source information, and leaves renv startup activation in place. A migration command could handle those steps as part of a supported transition.

A small user-facing interface could be:

```sh
rig proj renv migrate --dry-run
rig proj renv migrate
```

The preview would show the dependency conversion, startup-file edits, installation plan, and any unsupported sources or conflicting configuration. The migration would then:

1. Use the existing `renv.lock` as its input, preserving exact R and package versions and translating supported package sources. Stop with an explanation if a source cannot be represented faithfully, rather than silently substituting a package from another source.
2. Resolve and install the rig environment, reporting any differences or failures before completing the startup handoff.
3. Back up the startup files it changes and replace renv activation with rig's library setup, preserving unrelated settings. Retain `renv.lock`, the old project library, and renv's global cache.
4. Report what changed, how to recover the previous setup, which R version the editor needs to use, and how to check the environment. Users would still run their own analysis or tests to establish that results match.

Migration should not automatically snapshot the current renv library: choosing whether the installed environment or the existing lock file represents the intended state belongs to the user. It should also keep migration separate from package upgrades.

### How would this differ from `import`?

`rig proj renv import` already creates a manifest and startup boilerplate, so it is more than a file converter. However, treating another project's lock file as dependency input is a different intent from replacing the environment manager of a working project. Keeping separate commands would make those side effects explicit:

| Responsibility | `rig proj renv import` | Proposed `rig proj renv migrate` |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | Bring dependency declarations into a rig project. | Switch a working renv project to rig. |
| Version policy | Make preserving exact versions versus importing compatible ranges an explicit choice. | Preserve exact versions by default. |
| Package sources | Translate supported sources or report what cannot be imported. | Require faithful translation before proceeding. |
| Resolve and install | Leave these as separate operations. | Include locking and syncing in the migration. |
| renv activation | Leave the existing activation alone. | Manage the startup handoff with safeguards. |
| Recovery | Refuse accidental overwrites. | Back up changed startup files and retain the old environment. |

The version-policy and source-handling entries above are suggested improvements to `import`, not descriptions of its current behavior. Source translation should be shared by both commands: users should not have to choose `migrate` to avoid losing a Git or private-repository source. An exact-version import option could support the same preservation policy without changing the existing compatible-range default.

The aim would be to automate the mechanical migration steps while leaving project-specific decisions and validation visible.

title: Use rig in the setup-r action
description:
Similar to #403, but for `setup-r` instead of `setup-r-dependencies`: what it would take for [`r-lib/actions/setup-r`](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/tree/v2-branch/setup-r) to install R with rig.

rig already does the core of what `setup-r` does (resolving the version, installing R, Rtools, links, repos, user library). Most of the remaining work is glue in the action. A possible plan is to ship it as an opt-in `installer: rig` input first, and switch the default later.

## Background

rig already does the core of what `setup-r` does: resolving a version,
installing R, Rtools, quick links, and repos. The open question is what rig
itself is missing before `setup-r` could install R via rig instead of its own
three installers.

## Missing rig features

- [x] **`--json` output for `rig add`.** Needed so the action can read back
  the installed version and path without a separate `rig resolve --json` /
  `rig list --json` call.
- [ ] **Windows install-dir override for admin mode.** rig installs into
  `C:\Program Files\R`; `setup-r` and many existing workflows expect
  `C:\R`. Without an override, switching a workflow to rig is a breaking
  change for anything that hard-codes the old path.
- [ ] **A way to print/export Rtools environment info.** `rig add rtools`
  installs Rtools and wires it into `Renviron.site`, but shell steps in a
  workflow also need Rtools on `PATH`, plus `RTOOLSxx_HOME` and
  `_R_INSTALL_TIME_PATCHES_=no` exported into the job environment. rig has
  no command to surface these values today.
- [ ] **`rig add gfortran` on macOS.** `setup-r` downloads one of three
  gfortran/flang variants depending on R version and arch, plus sets
  `SDKROOT`. rig has no equivalent.
- [ ] **Extra repositories in `rig repos setup`.** `setup-r` writes RSPM,
  CRAN, and `extra-repositories` into `~/.Rprofile`. rig's repo setup only
  covers P3M and CRAN in the site profile; it needs a way to add extra repos
  (tracked together with the broader repos work in #403).
- [ ] **`R_LIBS_USER`.** rig does not set this outside of rvenv projects, so
  whoever replaces `setup-r`'s installer still needs to set it. Worth
  confirming on an actual runner whether rig should set a default here.

## Compatibility gaps to check, not build

- [ ] **Version string parsing.** `setup-r` special-cases inputs like `3`,
  `3.x`, `4.x.x`. Confirm `rig resolve` / `rig add` accept the same forms, or
  this mapping has to stay in the action.
- [ ] **Platform coverage vs. `setup-r`.** Confirm how far back rig supports
  each OS (e.g. R 3.x on macOS and Windows), and whether rig handles the R
  3.6 P3M snapshot pin that `setup-r` currently applies.

## Out of scope for rig (stays in the action regardless)

For reference, these are things `setup-r` does that are not rig's job and
would remain action-side glue even after the features above land:
qpdf/ghostscript/devscripts/checkbashisms installs, the `addPath` /
`RTOOLS*_HOME` export step itself, `TZ` / `NOT_CRAN` / `RSPM` /
`RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE` env vars, and getting the `rig` binary onto the
runner.

## What we gain

- About 600 lines of installer code removed from the action: version resolution, the three installers, Rtools selection.
- Multiple R versions in one job.
- Windows arm64 and Rtools handling in one place.
- Portable Linux builds for unsupported distros.
- The same R setup in CI as users have locally.
- Having rig on the runner is needed for #403 anyway.

## Risks

- [ ] Behavior changes affect many workflows. Ship as opt-in `installer: rig`, run both code paths through the r-lib/actions test matrix (`oldrel-4`, `devel`, `next`, arm64, containers), then switch the default.
- [ ] Check how far back rig supports each platform (R 3.x on macOS and Windows) against what `setup-r` supports now. Also the R 3.6 P3M snapshot pin.
- [ ] Pin the rig version in the action, so a rig release cannot break CI.

title: Use rig in setup-r-dependencies
description:
## Gaps (roughly by importance)

- [x] #426
  No sysreqs lookup/install at all. pak's biggest CI feature. 
  Needs: sysreqs DB (P3M sysreqs API or r-hub/r-system-requirements rules), distro
  detection (already exists for installing R), sudo handling, `apt-get update`.
- [x] #428
  No `bioc::` refs, no Bioc repos, no Bioc-version-to-R-version mapping.
- [ ] **Configured / extra repositories.** `pkg` and `proj` use only P3M/CRAN (help note in
  `src/help/pkg-install.md`, `repos-plan.md`). Missing: r-universe, drat, `Additional_repositories`,
  repos from `setup-r`'s `extra-repositories`.
- [ ] **`Config/Needs/<x>` for `rig pkg install`.** Only `proj import` reads them
  (`src/proj.rs:493`), and even there groups are "carried but not solved" per
  `src/help/proj-import.md:41` (conflicts with `proj-lock.md`). CI needs `--needs check`,
  `--needs website`, etc.
- [ ] **pak ref syntax `any::` and `deps::`.** Not parsed (`src/pkgsource.rs:106`). Existing
  workflows use them everywhere; `any::x` could map to plain `x`, `deps::path` to
  `--no-install-project path`.
- [ ] **Finer dependency selection.** Only hard vs `--dev` (Suggests + Enhances). pak allows
  `"hard"`, `TRUE`, `"all"`, explicit field lists, `Config/Needs/*`. Enhances are often
  unavailable; `--dev` may need `--ignore-unavailable` in CI where pak just works.
- [ ] **Lock-then-install split for caching.** Need a stable resolution file to hash for the cache
  key (e.g. `rig pkg install --dry-run --lockfile out.lock`, then `--from-lockfile`), or a
  documented, cacheable rig cache dir (`rig cache info --json` path) as alternative.
  The resolution must be deterministic for the same inputs.
- [ ] **Working with the R that `setup-r` installs.** `setup-r` uses its own installers
  (r-builds in `/opt/R` on Linux, CRAN pkg on macOS, CRAN exe on Windows); rig must find
  them, honor `R_LIBS_USER` set by the action, and work with system R (`/usr/lib/R`, e.g.
  rocker images) and in containers without sudo. Needs checking.
- [ ] **Upgrade semantics.** rig always picks newest; pak default `upgrade = FALSE` keeps
  installed versions that satisfy constraints. Matters with restored caches and
  `lockfile-create-lib`.
- [ ] **GitHub auth.** No `GITHUB_PAT`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` support; relies on git credentials.
  Fine for public repos; private `Remotes:` in CI need a token-to-git bridge.
- [ ] **Windows source builds.** Relies on Rtools being present and found; confirm rig's
  `R CMD INSTALL` path works on GitHub runners.
- [ ] **Nice to have / could stay in the action:** pandoc and quarto install, session info
  print (a `rig pkg list` with sources and versions table is close), failure log dumps
  (rig already points to `_logs`; CI wants the log printed inline).
- [ ] **The action itself.** A `setup-rig-dependencies` (or new mode of the existing action)
  that wires rig + `actions/cache` together with the same inputs, so workflows switch
  with a one-line change.

``` text
...
ld: warning: -single_module is obsolete

``` shell

title: Environment variable for centralised project libraries
description:
I've been reading over the new `rig proj` functionality. I know it's currently experimental. It looks very helpful!

The most useful thing for us in my organisation would be if rig had support for a centralised project library location and this location could be set using an environment variable.

From what I can see, this isn't mentioned in the existing docs, although it is hinted at. It looks like `rig proj sync`  allows one to set `--library`, but without the option of an environment variable and presumably without the destination location being managed. 

We would like functionality similar to what renv currently provides in ` RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY_ROOT`  and ` RENV_PATHS_CACHE` environment variables.

The current default of `rig proj sync --library` which is ".rvenv/lib" clashes with the executable scanning our organisation has set up. For more details, you can see a [similar request which made it's way through the uv project](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/1495).

title: Install to custom (user) directory
description:
- [ ] Windows
- [ ] macOS
- [ ] Linux

## Windows

On Windows, this seems easy. It is possible that we'll need to replace Rscript.exe, see below at macOS.

## macOS

* On macOS we can set `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` in the `R` startup script:
    ```
    # export DYLD_PRINT_LIBRARIES=1
    R_HOME_DIR=/Users/gaborcsardi/R/R-4.5.3
    R_HOME_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0" 2>/dev/null || realpath "$0" 2>/dev/null || echo "$0")")/.." && pwd)"
    export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH="${R_HOME_DIR}/lib"
    ```

    Positron can't handle this (yet), so temporarily we'll set `R_HOME_DIR` to a constant first, because this is what Positron parses from the `R` file.

* We'll also need to update the hardcoded paths in some script files. 

* The most hacky part is working around the install path being hardcoded into the Rscript binary. We'll need to replace that with a shell script that sets `RHOME`, which Rscript uses to override the R home, and then calls the original Rscript binary.

AFAICT there is no need to patch the binaries with `install_name_tool`, because `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` takes precedence even over absolute paths. Using `install_name_tool` and `otool` is not great, anyway, because they are not part of a vanilla macOS installation.

Similarly, AFAICT there is no need to patch CRAN binary packages after `install.packages()`, either. CRAN binaries work  OOTB, without patching.

## Linux

* The difficulty here is the system packages. We need to use the local package manage (i.e. apt, dpkg, etc) to download system packages and install them into the R installation. Based on some quick tests, this is possible. We'll need to create some symlinks for BLAS/LAPACK, otherwise it is pretty straightforward, at least on Debian/Ubuntu.

* We'll need to update the hardcoded paths in scripts.

* We need to replace Rscript with a script, as discussed above for macOS.

title: Sign windows installer
Positron settings.json is JSONC, but rig parses it with serde_json
description:
### Problem

`ensure_positron_custom_root_folders()` parses Positron's `settings.json` with
`serde_json::from_str`:

https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/main/src/common.rs#L579-L584

```rust
let mut settings: serde_json::Value = if settings_path.exists() {
    let contents = std::fs::read_to_string(&settings_path)?;
    serde_json::from_str(&contents)?
} else {
    serde_json::Value::Object(serde_json::Map::new())
};
```

VS Code family settings files are **JSONC**, not JSON. `//` and `/* */` comments and
trailing commas are all legal there, VS Code's own settings editor accepts them, and
plenty of real user `settings.json` files contain them. `serde_json` rejects all of
them, so on such a file the function returns `Err` and rig never registers `r_root` in
`positron.r.customRootFolders`.

The failure is reported — every caller does

```rust
if let Err(e) = ensure_positron_custom_root_folders() {
    OUTPUT.warn(&format!("Could not update Positron settings: {}", e));
    warn!("Could not update Positron settings: {}", e);
}
```

(`src/macos.rs:188`, `src/macos.rs:1907`, `src/linux.rs:336`, `src/linux.rs:1098`,
`src/windows/mod.rs:402`, `src/windows/mod.rs:1907`)

but the message is a raw serde parse error along the lines of `expected value at line 2
column 3`. It does not tell the user that a comment in their settings file is the cause,
and it scrolls past in the middle of an otherwise successful `rig add`. The practical
outcome is that Positron silently does not see the rig-installed R versions, and the user
has no obvious way to connect that to the warning.

### Reproduce

In user mode, with Positron installed:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/pos/Positron/User
printf '{\n  // my settings\n  "editor.fontSize": 13\n}\n' > /tmp/pos/Positron/User/settings.json
VSCODE_APPDATA=/tmp/pos rig add release
```

`positron.r.customRootFolders` is not written, and a `Could not update Positron settings`
warning appears. Removing the comment line makes the same command work.

### Suggested fix

Parse leniently. Either strip comments and trailing commas before handing the text to
`serde_json`, or use a JSONC-aware parser. Writing back with
`serde_json::to_string_pretty` already discards any comments the user had, which is a
separate (and arguably worse) wrinkle — a JSONC-preserving edit, or an in-place edit that
only touches the one key, would be friendlier than rewriting the whole file.

Failing that, at minimum: detect a parse error and emit an actionable message naming the
file and suggesting the cause, rather than surfacing the serde error verbatim.

### Notes

Found while sketching a VS Code / Positron extension for rig
(#356). The extension would not hit this,
because going through `workspace.getConfiguration().update()` lets VS Code do the JSONC
handling — which is an argument for the editor-side integration owning this key
eventually, but the CLI path should still work on its own.

title: macOS: do not change the default version when installing
description:
This is hard because the installer simply overwrites the symbolic link. One possible solution is creating a volume, installing there, removing the link, and then moving the files to the `/` volume.

Another possible way is to extract the `.pkg` file with `pkgutil --extract`, removing the symlink, and then pack it back up with `pkgutil --flatten`. Well, except that the contents is in a big `Payload` file after extracting, which is a cpio file, so we would need to remove it from that. Also, if there is some integrity check on the `.pkg` then this will not work.

A technically worse but probably good enough approach is to watch the disk while the installer is running and as soon as the `/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/Current` link is (re)created, we set it back to the previous default.

title: Multiple installations of the same R version
description:
Hi

Thanks for the great tool, I think this will make lots of people's lives easier 🎉 ! I have been playing around with getting two installations of the same R version to work. Probably a fairly niche thing so not suggesting you add it as a feature (unless there is demand) but thought I would post my solution in case it was helpful to anyone (and in case there are issues I haven't come across yet). My use case is to have two versions of R 4.2 installed, one with Bioconductor release (for analysis) and one with Bioconductor devel (for development) and to be able to switch between the two as needed.

These are the steps that worked for me on MacOS:

1. Install the desired R version.

```shell
rim install release
```

2. Rename the installed directory

```shell
mv /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.2 /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.2-bioc
```

3. Modify the main R script so that all paths point to the new location

```shell
vim /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.2-bioc/Resources/bin/R
```

Search for all occurrences of the installed R version and modify them to match the new path (eg. change all `4.2` to `4.2-bioc`)

4. Modify the base `Renviron` file to set the default user library path

  ```shell
  vim /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.2-bioc/Resources/etc/Renviron
  ```

  Find where `R_LIBS_USER` is set and modify it to point to the new installation directory.
  
  ```

title: rig rm does not clean all stale registry entries
description:
* `rig add 4.2.0` will install R and add to registry 
````
R-core
 > R <- Current Version and Install Path set to 4.2.0
   > 4.2.0 <- Current Version and Install Path set to 4.2.0
 > R64 <- Current Version and Install Path set to 4.2.0
   > 4.2.0 <- Current Version and Install Path set to 4.2.0
````

* `rig rm 4.2.0` will uninstall R and clean part of the registry which will be after 
```
R-core
 > R <- Current Version and Install Path set to 4.2.0
 > R64 <- Current Version and Install Path set to 4.2.0
```

So default version is sill set to the uninstall version. `rig system clean-registry` does not help (I guess this is what is called in the first place)

If we install several versions, and change default and then uninstall the one set as default, the default version in registry will still be the one uninstalled

* `rig add 4.2.0` is doing as describe above
* `rig add 4.1.2` will add 4.1.2 entry in registry
* `rig default 4.1.2` will modify the registry default version -> Current Version and Install Path are set to 4.1.2
* `rig rm 4.1.2` will uninstall and remove 4.1.2 from registry, but not from default R version where state will be
```
R-core
 > R <- Current Version and Install Path set to 4.1.2 which does not exists anymore 
   > 4.2.0 <- Current Version and Install Path set to 4.2.0
 > R64 <- Current Version and Install Path set to 4.1.2 which does not exists anymore 
   > 4.2.0 <- Current Version and Install Path set to 4.2.0
````
* `rig default 4.2.0` fix the problem


So it is possible to be in a state where the default version information is not the correct one. 
Found while trying to debug Quarto to find R installation when manage by `rig`

title: Error on brew upgrade (probably the cleanup part)
description:
Around a month ago, I encountered an issue while performing a `brew upgrade`. The specific error thrown was:

```
Error: Permission denied @ rb_readlink - /usr/local/bin/R-4.3-x86_64
```

To fix this, I used rig to:

- Uninstall all versions of R.
- Reinstall the latest version of R 

I made very sure to not run any sudo before this, but rig still asked for my password, so it is probably doing that internally.

After these steps, brew upgrade seemed fine, and I did not report the bug immediately, in order to keep down the noise on the issue tracker in case this was just due to me running with the wrong permissions initially. But there was a bit of worry in the back of my mind about it happening again. And, as fate would have it, the issue popped up again today, pretty much a month and a day later. And I'm guessing it is because it now tried to run cleanup again.

My guess is that `rig` with it's `sudo` permissions installs some files that homebrew thinks should be cleaned up. The permissions then cause homebrew cleanup to fail, so it gets rerun immediately and fails again. Uninstalling R monthly to enable brew cleanup seems overkill. If there is not an easy fix to `rig` itself, I wonder if there are any potential manual file permission workarounds that could be used to allow the cleanup to proceed successfully.

Would appreciate any insights or help with this. Thanks!

title: CRAN repository set by rig is to aggressive; overrides all RStudio settings
description: When rig sets the CRAN repository, it does so by adding: ```r options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org/")) ``` to `library/base/R/Rprofile`. This setting is very aggressive; it cannot be disabled (not even by running with `R --vanilla`), and because it is set after R starts up, it overwrites RStudio's CRAN settings. Using any `rig` version of R will cause warnings to appear in RStudio's Packages options, and the options that control CRAN repositories will not work with any `rig` version of R. I would propose the following: 1. Before setting the CRAN repository, check to see if it's set to something that appears intentional (e.g. not `@CRAN@`). If it appears to be intentionally set, leave it alone instead overwriting the user's preference. 2. Move the CRAN repository setting from the base library `Rprofile` to a regular R startup script, such as `Rprofile.site`. When diagnosing where the CRAN repository is getting set, absolutely no one is going to think to check in the base library. 3. Set an attribute on the options value to indicate `rig` as the origin of the setting. See also: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/13957

https://github.com/r-lib/pak/issues/61

Quick notes from our discussion today: we only need to make a best effort here, installing as many packages as we many, and clearly reporting on what we couldn't. The dependency solver is an optimiser, so we can pick the solution that is the best, and know that we're getting the best possible resolution.

title: Windows user mode: an alias link outside the current R root makes rig add/list fail
description:
On Windows in user mode, `rig add`, `rig list`, and the other commands that go through `sc_get_list_details()` stop with

```
Error: Cannot extract R version from C:\Users\<user>\.local\bin\R-release.exe, invalid R link file?
```

whenever any `R-release.exe`/`R-oldrel.exe`/`R-next.exe` link in the binary directory points at an R that is not under the current user root. macOS and Linux skip such a link instead. Seen with rig 0.11.0; the code is the same in v0.11.1 and on `main`.

## Reproduce

With a user-mode install and its alias links in `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin` (e.g. `R-release.exe` -> `%APPDATA%\rig\data\r\4.5.1\bin\R.exe`), point rig at another root:

```
set RIG_R_INSTALL_DIR=D:\R
rig list --user
rig add 4.3.3 --user
```

Both fail with the error above. The same happens when `RIG_R_INSTALL_DIR` names the default root but with forward slashes (`C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Roaming/rig/data/r`), since the match below is a plain string prefix test, and after switching `r-install-dir` in the config while the old links remain.

## Cause

`find_aliases()` propagates any error from `find_r_version_in_link()` with `?` ([src/windows/mod.rs#L1350](https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/v0.11.1/src/windows/mod.rs#L1350)). In user mode, `find_r_version_in_link()` requires the link target to start with `get_r_root()` plus a backslash, and bails otherwise ([src/windows/mod.rs#L1372-L1396](https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/v0.11.1/src/windows/mod.rs#L1372-L1396)). So one alias link into a different root takes down the whole listing, and with it `rig add`'s already-installed check ([src/windows/mod.rs#L390](https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/v0.11.1/src/windows/mod.rs#L390)) before anything is downloaded. `rig system make-links` reads the links the same way ([src/windows/mod.rs#L1290](https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/v0.11.1/src/windows/mod.rs#L1290)).

On Linux ([src/linux.rs#L1335](https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/v0.11.1/src/linux.rs#L1335)) and macOS ([src/macos.rs#L933](https://github.com/r-lib/rig/blob/v0.11.1/src/macos.rs#L933)), `find_aliases()` does `None => continue` when a link's version cannot be worked out, so an alias into another root is simply not reported.

## Suggested fix

Have the Windows `find_aliases()` skip (with a `debug!`) a link whose target is outside the root instead of failing, matching the other platforms. `rig add` would then install into the requested root, and `rig default`/`rig system fix-aliases` would re-point the links as usual.

## Context

This is behind rstudio/rstudio#19468: RStudio runs the bundled rig with `RIG_R_INSTALL_DIR` set to the destination the user confirmed. rstudio/rstudio#19476 fixes the forward-slash case on RStudio's side, but a destination other than the folder the existing links point into still fails until rig tolerates the link.
